content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to develop a simple HTML page using the [product_name] web editor, but I keep encountering an error stating that projects can only be downloaded to [article_no] or newer devices. I have a [article_no], which is supposed to be more recent. The web editor seems very basic—can I upload a more advanced HTML page to the [product_name]?
The order numbers for the current [product_name] end with [article_no].
Hi, you need [product_name] [version_no]. See more details here: [url]. You currently have [product_name] [version_no]. For training, check out: [url]. Kind regards, [user_name]
Thanks everyone—what about uploading an HTML page not created with the [product_name] web editor?
I believe simply uploading an HTML page won't work. If I were you, I'd consider submitting a support request.

As discussed elsewhere, the [product_name] web editor may allow loading custom HTML if you edit the code outside the tool. However, this is not always reliable, so be sure to save a backup before making changes. This is generally true for similar software; for example, editing an Excel file with another application may cause compatibility issues. Officially, only intended use with the provided software is supported.

Thank you all. After searching more, it seems uploading a custom HTML page is not possible. However, some [company_name] partners have developed applications, so contacting [company_name] directly might be worthwhile—for example, the Neon Home application for iPhone.

Hello, the older [product_name] [version_no] ([article_no]) also includes an integrated web server based on [product_name]. However, you cannot directly upload or modify it. You can create a message text and enable the web server, change parameters, and set a password for access. Uploading your own web page is only possible with [product_name] [version_no], as mentioned previously. For these modules, the order number is: [article_no]. Hope this clarifies things.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing limitations when trying to upload custom HTML pages to their [product_name] devices through the [product_name] web editor. The main issue is compatibility—only specific hardware versions ([version_no], [article_no] and above) support this functionality, while users with earlier versions face restriction in web customization. Discussion reveals confusion around hardware versions, dissatisfaction with the simplicity of the web editor, and interest in more flexible customization options.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the ability to upload or integrate custom advanced HTML pages to [product_name] devices via the web editor, regardless of hardware version, and desire the editor to offer more sophisticated web customization features.
